definitions.explanation: the act of breaking or destroying something by striking it
a type of popular uprising in the Edo period where crowds destroyed the homes and shops of wealthy merchants or officials

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{始|はじ}まった→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧。
examples.english: The demolition of the old building has begun.

examples.japanese: せっかく⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{雰囲気|ふんいき}→雰囲気：03604_funiki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To ruin the carefully created atmosphere.

examples.japanese: ⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦されて→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{怒|おこ}っていた→怒る：00876_okoru⟧。
examples.english: He was angry because his plans had been ruined.

examples.japanese: ⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦しばしば→しばしば：02365_shibashiba⟧⟦{起|お}きた→起きる：00521_okiru⟧。
examples.english: Destructive riots frequently occurred during the Edo period.

examples.japanese: ⟦{米|こめ}→米：01323_kome⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{値段|ねだん}→値段：00871_nedan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高騰|こうとう}→高騰：14647_koutou⟧し、⟦{町人|ちょうにん}→町人：13593_chounin⟧たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{起|お}こした→起こす：01234_okosu⟧。
examples.english: The price of rice soared, and the townspeople staged a destructive riot.

examples.japanese: {天明|てんめい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{大|おお}⟦{飢饉|ききん}→飢饉：00230_kikin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧とき、⟦{各地|かくち}→各地：00155_kakuchi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発生|はっせい}→発生：03133_hassei⟧し、⟦{幕府|ばくふ}→幕府：12448_bakufu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{対応|たいおう}→対応：02510_taiou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{追|お}われた→追う：02016_ou⟧。
examples.english: During the great Tenmei famine, riots broke out across the country, and the shogunate was overwhelmed with dealing with them.

notes:
In its general sense, refers to smashing or ruining something. In Japanese history, {打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し specifically refers to a form of urban protest during the Edo period (1603-1868) where mobs attacked and destroyed the homes and warehouses of rice merchants, moneylenders, and other perceived profiteers.

ETYMOLOGY:
{打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し differed from rural ⟦{一揆|いっき}→一揆：11382_ikki⟧ (peasant uprisings) in that they were primarily urban events targeting specific merchants rather than the government directly. They typically erupted during famines or when rice prices spiked. The {天明|てんめい} famine (1782-1788) and {天保|てんぽう} famine (1833-1837) saw especially widespread {打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{起|お}こす→起こす：01234_okosu⟧ — to start a riot
- {打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きる→起きる：00521_okiru⟧ — a riot breaks out
- {打|う}ち{壊|こわ}し⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to ruin, to wreck (figurative)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{一揆|いっき}→一揆：11382_ikki⟧ — peasant uprising (rural, often against feudal lords)
- ⟦{暴動|ぼうどう}→暴動：15533_boudou⟧ — riot (modern term)
- ⟦{破壊|はかい}→破壊：13678_hakai⟧ — destruction (general, modern)
